blocks.html: One might here raise some difficulty, and think that one ought not to give great faith to the last deposition of these witnesses, who depart from the first: both because they have varied a, and thus, by the contradiction and repugnance of their depositions, themselves overthrow it b; and because also they are perjured, and the testimony of a perjurer, as everyone understands, ought to be rejected c; especially since, if any faith could be given to one of their depositions, it would have to be to the first, made with oath d. But all these difficulties can easily be resolved if one comes to consider that it is very reasonable that a witness who, through error and the circumvention of another, has deposed falsely should, as soon as his error appears to him, correct himself e: and thus not only on the spot, or shortly after (as is indubitably permitted him f), but even after a long space and interval of time, if until then he had not perceived his error, or else some other just cause newly presents itself h. The judgment of which, together with the distance of time, is wholly referred to the discretion of the judge i. Otherwise, if the witness, for his pleasure and of his own free will, long after his deposition wished to depart from it, and to change or correct what he had already deposed, he would not be received to do so, for fear of subornation k.

notes.citation: Digest 22.5 (De testibus), l. 2 (D. 22.5.2, Modestinus) and l. Qui falso (D. 22.5.16, Paul); Code 9.22 (Ad legem Corneliam de falsis), l. Eos (fragment not identified)
notes.original: l. ij l. qui falſo. D. de te ſtib. l. eos. C. de falſ.
notes.gloss: D. 22.5.2: witnesses who waver against the faith of their own testimony are not to be heard; D. 22.5.16: those who have given false or varying testimony, or betrayed both parties, are punished by the judges.

notes.citation: Digest 36.2 (Quando dies legatorum vel fideicommissorum cedat), the penultimate law, § 1 as printed — the penultimate fragment, D. 36.2.30 (Labeo, Quod pupillae legatum est), has no § 1 and nothing on contradictory statements; unidentified
notes.original: l. penultieme. P. j. D. quand. dies l. ced.
notes.gloss: Cited for the rule that statements which contradict one another destroy one another. The P. stands for the paragraph sign.

notes.citation: Decretals, X 2.20 (De testibus et attestationibus), c. Testimonium (X 2.20.54); Accursius (Accurſe), the Gloss on Digest 3.2 (De his qui notantur infamia), l. Lucius (D. 3.2.21, Paul, Lucius Titius crimen intendit), and on Digest 22.5 (De testibus), l. 3, § Lege Iulia (D. 22.5.3.5, Callistratus; the print's l. ni. read as l. iij.)
notes.original: c. teſtimonium. de teſt, Accurſe en la l. Lucius. D. de iis qui not. infa. & à la l. ni. P lege Iul. D. de teſt.
notes.gloss: The perjured and the infamous are excluded from testimony; D. 22.5.3.5 recites the exclusions of the lex Iulia.

notes.citation: Decretals, X 2.20 (De testibus et attestationibus), c. Sicut (X 2.20.9, Alexander III)
notes.gloss: Of two depositions, the sworn one is preferred.

notes.citation: Decretals, X 2.20 (De testibus et attestationibus), c. Praeterea (X 2.20.27, Celestine III; the chapter is cited again at {h}, {i} and {k}); Accursius (Accurſe) on the Authenticum, Novel 90 (De testibus), collatio 7, at § Quia vero; Bartolus (Bartole) and the others on l. Eos, cited above at {a}
notes.original: Preterea c. de teſt. Accur ſe au P. quia verò, de teſt. aux. nou
notes.gloss: ?]lles: ſous la col lation vij. Bar tole & les au tres en la l. eos alleguee. [A witness who has deposed in error may correct his deposition; the print's nou[?]lles is nouuelles, the Novels, and ſous la collation vij places Novel 90 in the seventh collatio of the Authenticum, where it stands.

notes.citation: Liber Sextus, VI 5.2 (De haereticis), c. Accusatus, § Licet (VI 5.2.8.3, Boniface VIII, Licet vero periuri)
notes.original: c. accuſatus. P. licet. de hæreti. au vj.
notes.gloss: On witnesses in causes of heresy who retract or amend their testimony, and when they are heard.

notes.citation: The Gloss on a chapter of Decretals, X 2.28 (De appellationibus), printed c. au ſit (perhaps c. Cum sit; chapter not identified); the Doctors on c. Praeterea (X 2.20), cited above at {e}
notes.original: Gloſe au c. au ſit. de appella Les Docteurs au c. præterea. deſ ſus allegué.
notes.gloss: The appraisal of the cause and of the lapse of time is left to the judge.

notes.citation: The Doctors on l. Eos (C. 9.22) and on c. Praeterea (X 2.20), both cited above at {a} and {e}
notes.original: les docteurs, en la l. eos. & au c. præterea. alleguez.
notes.gloss: A witness is not allowed to change his deposition at pleasure, lest he be suborned to it.

notes.citation: Panormitanus (Niccolò de' Tudeschi, Panorme) and the others on c. Praeterea (X 2.20), cited above at {e}
notes.original: Panorme & les autre au c. præterea allegué.
notes.gloss: The just causes for which a witness may be re-examined and may amend what he has said.
